name: Today's Report
headline: Rates sit at 7.17% as futures traders lift the odds of a December Fed hike to about 82%.
teaser: Mortgage News Daily's 30-year average is 7.17% and the 15-year 6.83%. Those are Friday's rates; Monday's reading posts this afternoon. The 30-year is 0.10 lower than a week ago and 0.39 lower than a month ago (7.56%). At 7.17%, a Fremont buyer at today's $1,286,500 median with 20% down would pay about $6,965 a month in principal and interest, $274 less than at last month's rate.

sections.label: Real estate
sections.html:
Mortgage News Daily's 30-year average is 7.17% and the 15-year 6.83%. Those are Friday's rates; Monday's reading posts this afternoon. The 30-year is 0.10 lower than a week ago and 0.39 lower than a month ago (7.56%). At 7.17%, a Fremont buyer at today's $1,286,500 median with 20% down would pay about $6,965 a month in principal and interest, $274 less than at last month's rate.

The strong jobs report (see Economy) is still working through the Fed outlook. By our math from fed funds futures at 9:00 AM PT, traders now put the chance of a quarter point increase at the December 9 meeting at about 82%, up from the high 70s after Friday's settlement. The Fed's target range is 3.75% to 4.00%. The Fed does not set mortgage rates; they follow the 10-Year Treasury, which is near 4.88% this morning, about where it was Friday.

The board wide table is 2,451, from 2,456 in Saturday's report, with 140 coming soon and 157 brand new. The five city ledger is 624, from 625: Newark (78) fell two and Hayward (178) one, Milpitas (94) and Union City (62) added one each, and Fremont (212) held. Fremont's median on market list price eased to $1,286,500 from $1,298,000.

What this means for you: if you are under contract or close to it, ask your lender what a lock through early December would cost, since the Fed meets December 9. Every quarter point on the median Fremont home is about $175 a month. Sellers, 175 homes in our five cities have now been listed 60 days or longer, up from 163 in Saturday's report.

  • Board wide: 2,451 listings across our 15 city table, counting active and in contract together, with 140 coming soon and 157 brand new.

Alameda County (Fremont Focus)

  • Live ledger: 624 listings across Fremont, Hayward, Milpitas, Newark and Union City. 560 are on the market and 64 are coming soon.
  • Fremont: 212 live, 168 active, 28 coming soon and 15 brand new. The median on market list price is $1,286,500 at $802 a square foot, and the typical active listing has been out 35 days.
  • The rest of the ledger: Hayward 178, Milpitas 94, Newark 78, Union City 62.
  • Across all five cities the median is $1,022,475 at $665 a square foot. 278 homes are priced under a million, and 175 have been sitting 60 days or longer.

sections.label: Economy
sections.html:
Here is the jobs story in one picture (chart). Employers added 165,000 jobs in October, nearly three times the 59,000 that economists surveyed by Dow Jones expected, after 186,000 in August and 60,000 in September, the Bureau of Labor Statistics said. Unemployment eased to 4.1% from 4.2%. September and October are first estimates, and BLS revises each month twice.

Oil is the big mover this morning. Brent futures are down about 4.5% to $93.86 at 9:13 AM PT; the card shows Friday's settlement of $98.32 because today's price has not settled. Gold is up 1.11% to $4,120.20 and silver 1.60% to $52.77 against Friday's settlements. The 10-Year is near 4.88%, up about 0.02 from Treasury's 4.86% close Friday.

Market Briefs did not arrive this morning, so every number in this report comes straight from its source.

images.alt: Bar chart of the net change in U.S. nonfarm payroll jobs: August 2026 up 186,000, September up 60,000 and October up 165,000. A dashed line marks the October forecast of 59,000 from economists surveyed by Dow Jones; October came in about 2.8 times the forecast.
images.caption: Employers added 165,000 jobs in October, nearly three times the 59,000 economists expected.
images.source: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, Employment Situation, October 2026; forecast: Dow Jones survey of economists, via CNBC

sections.label: Stocks
sections.html:
Stocks are bouncing back to start the week. At 9:13 AM PT the S&P 500 is up 2.27% at 7,544.41, the Nasdaq 2.62% at 25,223.41 and the Dow 2.05%, or about 1,050 points, at 52,336.11. Even so, the S&P 500 is still about 1.9% below where it closed last Wednesday, before Thursday's selloff.

Chip stocks are leading the rebound. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index is up 6.62% and sits about 2.5% below its Wednesday close, after Thursday's 12.25% plunge. Two local names are near the top: Fremont's Lam Research is up 9.2% and Milpitas's KLA 8.9%. AMD is up 11.6%. Nvidia is the exception, down 4.9%.

Falling oil is helping too (see Economy).
